item.title: ESUT plans drug production to reduce import dependence
item.description: …VC seeks increased admission quota for Pharmacy programme The Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) has announced plans to establish pharmaceutical drug production facilities as part of efforts to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and strengthen local pharmaceutical manufacturing. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, disclosed this on Monday while receiving an accreditation team from the National Universities Commission (NUC) assessing the university’s Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Okolie said the proposed facilities would serve a dual purpose of contributing to domestic drug supply and providing students with practical training in pharmaceutical manufacturing. He urged pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical sector to embrace experiential learning and move beyond theoretical instruction to hands-on drug production, stressing the importance of building local capacity to meet the country’s pharmaceutical needs. According to him, establishing drug production facilities within the university would equip students with the practical skills required to compete in the pharmaceutical industry while supporting efforts to reduce reliance on imported medicines. The Vice-Chancellor said the university had prioritised the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences through the provision of critical infrastructure and scientific equipment to enhance teaching, learning and research. He also appealed to the NUC accreditation team to consider increasing the faculty’s existing admission quota, assuring the team of the university management’s full cooperation and support throughout the accreditation exercise. Earlier, the leader of the accreditation team, Prof. Florence Eichie, said the visit was not intended to witch-hunt the university but to assess the facilities and resources available for teaching and research in the Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) programme. Eichie explained that the exercise was designed to evaluate the university’s capacity to deliver quality pharmaceutical education in line with the NUC’s accreditation requirements. She solicited the cooperation of the university management, staff and students to ensure a smooth and successful exercise. item.title: ‘Not the solution’, ‘ludicrous’, Man Utd legends, English pundits react to Carrick’s sacking
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick after days of speculation over his future, following the club’s poor start to the Premier League season. The decision came after United’s hierarchy reviewed the team’s performances and considered possible replacements, with Mauricio Pochettino lined up for the job. But before the dismissal on Thursday, some prominent voices had questioned whether sacking Carrick would solve United’s problems, while others argued he should have been allowed to stay. United legends questioned whether a sacking would solve the problems Former United captain Gary Neville said changing managers would not address the club’s deeper issues. Speaking to NBC Sports, he warned that United risked repeating a cycle of brief improvement followed by a return to poor performances. Neville said eight managerial changes in 12 years showed that replacing the head coach alone was “not the answer”. He pointed to poor recruitment, weaknesses in the performance department and a lack of strong leadership throughout the club. Joined by his brother Gary on NBC Sports , former United defender Phil Neville focused on the defence after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, saying the back four that finished the match was not good enough for the Premier League and could get a manager sacked. Roy Keane had also criticised Carrick’s comments on Sky Sports after the Villa game, saying the head coach “talks a lot but doesn’t say much”. Keane questioned what would change if United continued conceding goals and chances. Paul Scholes, meanwhile, had looked ahead to United’s next appointment. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, he backed Antonio Conte over Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, while warning that Conte would come with “a big warning”. Other English pundits have their say as Carragher calls the prospect of sacking Carrick ‘ludicrous’ Former Liverpool captain Jamie Carragher had called the prospect of dismissing Carrick “ludicrous” before the decision was made. He argued Carrick should help United through a difficult period before the club appointed a top-level manager in the summer. Jamie Redknapp had earlier said the squad lacked the quality and structure needed to turn the season around, adding that Carrick needed help with the players available to him. Former England international Chris Waddle, speaking after United’s draw with Tottenham in September, said the team had lost confidence and needed to rebuild it. item.title: Triton cabin crew’s medical certificate invalid during mid-air door incident – NSIB
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, has disclosed that the flight crew of a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft, with nationality and registration marks T7-SEI, operated by Triton Aviation Limited, observed an abnormal increase in cabin altitude and suspected a pressurisation issue at 17:19, before its passenger-crew door detached during initial climb. NSIB also revealed that the cabin crew’s medical certificate was not valid at the time of that occurrence. Recall that on October 15, 2026, the serious incident occurred after the aircraft took-off from Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja. The aircraft, operating as DWC052, was conducting a non-scheduled flight from Abuja to Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, with nine persons on board, comprising two flight crew members, one cabin crew member and six passengers. NSIB, in its preliminary report, stated that the captain subsequently instructed the cabin crew to double-check the main cabin door, adding that as the cabin crew approached the passenger-crew door to carry out the inspection, the door opened and subsequently detached from the aircraft. Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of NSIB, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, who signed the report, stated that the flight crew subsequently declared an emergency and coordinated with Abuja Air Traffic Control, ATC, for an immediate return to the airport. The report reads: “The aircraft landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 17:34 local time. All nine occupants disembarked without injury. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. “Following notification of the occurrence on the same day, the NSIB immediately deployed investigators to the site to search for and recover the detached door, and commenced post-occurrence assessments. The detached door was subsequently recovered from a cornfield in Gui Village, Abuja Municipal Area Council, approximately five miles southwest of the airport. “The bureau reiterates that the preliminary report contains the factual information established during the investigation to date, including initial findings based on the evidence currently available and immediate safety recommendations arising from safety issues identified at this stage of the investigation. The report does not include analysis or conclusions regarding the causes or contributing factors associated with the occurrence, as the investigation remains ongoing. The bureau will publish its final report, including its analysis, conclusions, and further safety recommendations where appropriate, upon completion of the investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation.” The post Triton cabin crew’s medical certificate invalid during mid-air door incident – NSIB appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Members of the All Progressives Congress APC in Kano State have begun mobilising non-indigenes living in the state to vote for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf in the 2027 general elections. They inaugurated a political support group, Asiwaju Kano for Asiwaju Jagaban (AKA), which is led by Kogi lawmaker, Hon. Leke Abejide and has set for itself a target of at least 1.5 million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. The Chairman of the AKA Planning Committee, Hon. Ekundayo Emmanuel, said at the inauguration in Kano that coordinators had been installed in all 44 local government areas of the state. “Today, we are inaugurating coordinators across all 44 local government areas. Our responsibility is to mobilise at least one million five hundred thousand votes from non-indigenes residing across Kano State for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, our esteemed governor and leader, the people’s governor, Engineer Abba Kabir Yusuf, popularly known as Abba Gida Gida, as well as all APC candidates in the state,” he said. Emmanuel said the group was established to promote the political vision of Tinubu and Yusuf, adding that structures were being put in place to meet its target. The Kano State Coordinator of AKA, Hon. item.title: Nobody defended Peter Obi like Yunusa Tanko in the North — Shehu Sani
item.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Yunusa Tanko was one of the strongest advocates of Peter Obi in northern Nigeria, following his departure from the Obidient Movement and appointment to the Social Democratic Party’s 2027 presidential campaign council. Sani expressed surprise at Tanko’s decision to part ways with Obi, given his commitment to promoting the former Labour Party presidential candidate in the North. In a post on X on Wednesday, the former lawmaker wrote: “Nobody in the Northern part of River Niger has fanatically defended and promoted Dr Peter like Dr Yunusa Tanko. What must have happened for Dr Yunusa to part ways with Dr Peter? Anyway, nothing is impossible in politics.” Tanko, who previously coordinated the Obidient Movement, was on Wednesday named national coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election. His appointment was announced at the inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Abuja, where he pledged to work with its presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and running mate, Usman Bugaje, towards securing victory at the polls. Explaining his political realignment, Tanko said he resigned as political adviser (North) to Obi on October 30. He linked the decision to his appointment to the leadership of the National Consultative Front (NCFront), following the death of its former co-chairman and ex-Speaker of the House of Representatives, Ghali Na’Abba. Tanko also disclosed that he had contacted Obi and the National Democratic Congress leader, Seriake Dickson, to inform them of his decision. He acknowledged their support during his time as coordinator of the Obidient Movement and expressed appreciation for their contributions. The SDP campaign coordinator said his relationship with Adebayo predated the latest appointment, adding that they had worked together since 2023 and shared a commitment to building a better Nigeria. He also described the SDP as a left-wing, people-oriented party that represents the interests of ordinary Nigerians, particularly those he said had been neglected. item.title: Zamfara APC declares Hassan Dangaladima winner of rerun primary
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The All Progressives Congress (APC) has declared Hassan Umar Dangaladima winner of the rerun primary election for the Birnin Magaji/Kaura-Namoda Federal Constituency of Zamfara State. Dangaladima polled 9,416 votes to defeat his challenger, Aminu Sani Jaji, who scored 661 votes in the exercise. The result was announced in Gusau by Mustapha Muhammad, Acting Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee from the party’s National Headquarters, in the presence of party leaders and other stakeholders. Muhammad said the committee, having concluded its assessment of the exercise, was satisfied that Dangaladima secured the highest number of votes and was therefore duly declared winner of the rerun primary. Speaking shortly after his declaration, Dangaladima pledged to provide effective and meaningful representation for the constituency if elected to the House of Representatives in the 2027 general election. He called on APC members and supporters to unite behind him and other candidates of the party ahead of the polls. He also urged party supporters to work towards the success of the APC in the forthcoming general election. He made the call while speaking with journalists in Abuja on Thursday, following the release of the Federal Government’s Second Quarter 2026 Budget Implementation Report and President Bola Tinubu’s request for National Assembly approval of a fresh external borrowing plan. Tinubu had on Wednesday written to the House of Representatives, seeking approval to implement the external borrowing plan contained in the 2026 Appropriation Act to finance budgeted projects and consolidate the macroeconomic gains recorded by his administration. The Budget Implementation Report, released by the Budget Office of the Federation on November 7, showed that government revenue stood at approximately N11.9 trillion in the first half of 2026. The report also indicated that Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, its strongest quarterly expansion since the third quarter of 2024, while nominal Gross Domestic Product rose to N119.29 trillion. The growth was attributed to improved crude oil production and resilient activities in the non-oil sector. Reacting to the figures, Agbese commended the Ministers of Finance and Budget and Economic Planning, Taiwo Oyedele and Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, respectively, for their roles in strengthening fiscal coordination and improving budget performance. He said the figures underscored the importance of effective fiscal management, improved revenue generation and coordination in implementing national development priorities. “These numbers show that deliberate efforts are being made to improve the management of our economy. We must acknowledge the work being done by the Ministers of Finance and Budget and Economic Planning to strengthen fiscal coordination and ensure that national priorities are reflected in government spending. “While there is still considerable work to be done, we should be able to recognise progress where it is being made. The figures indicate that the economy is responding to ongoing reforms, and the responsibility before us is to sustain that momentum,” he said. The Labour Party lawmaker said collaboration between the two ministers was important to achieving the administration’s economic objectives, particularly in strengthening revenue generation, managing public expenditure and directing available resources towards critical sectors. He added that regular assessments of budget performance were necessary to identify implementation challenges, measure progress and ensure that public funds were deployed in line with approved priorities. On the proposed N10.8 trillion external borrowing, Agbese said the request should be considered within the context of the government’s financing requirements and the need to sustain critical infrastructure and development projects. He said the proposal also presented an opportunity for the executive and legislature to strengthen cooperation in addressing the country’s development financing needs. The lawmaker, however, urged ministries, departments and agencies to improve budget execution and accountability to ensure that approved allocations delivered measurable results. Agbese maintained that the success of government spending and borrowing should ultimately be measured by their impact on the living conditions of Nigerians. “The ultimate test of any budget or external borrowing plan is its impact on the lives of ordinary Nigerians. Beyond the figures, we want to see better roads, improved healthcare, quality education, jobs and opportunities for our people. That is why budget implementation must remain a priority,” he said. item.title: 2027: City Boy Movement targets 500,000 Enugu students for Tinubu
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The City Boy Movement has launched a membership registration drive across tertiary institutions in Enugu State, targeting 500,000 students as part of its mobilisation efforts for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. The South-East Zonal Coordinator of the movement’s Membership Registration and Data Management, Dr. Onyeka Nwafor, disclosed this during a membership registration exercise in Enugu. Nwafor said the movement had partnered with the Council of Students’ Union Government Presidents in Enugu State (COSPEN) to expand its membership base and mobilise students across campuses in support of Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He said the initiative was aimed at strengthening the movement’s presence in the South-East and demonstrating student support for the President’s administration. Also speaking, the COSPEN Chairman and President of the Students’ Union Government of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Comrade Emmanuel Nwankwo, said student leaders had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing the impact of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Nwankwo pledged that the council would mobilise more than 500,000 students for the registration exercise. He spoke during a meeting with Nwafor at Tiger Bar, Enugu, where both parties discussed strategies for expanding membership registration and improving coordination across campuses. “Many of our peers would have dropped out of school because of financial constraints, but NELFUND has eased the burden on parents and helped students remain in school. For this, we believe Mr President deserves a second term,” he said. Describing COSPEN as the gatekeepers of tertiary institutions in the state, Nwankwo said the student loan scheme had helped address some of the financial difficulties confronting students. Nwafor, a former governorship aspirant of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Anambra State, said the movement was determined to expand its presence across tertiary institutions in the South-East. “We have resolved to scale up registration across campuses in Enugu. The registration exercise will demonstrate the level of student support for President Tinubu’s administration, particularly the impact of the student loan initiative,” he said. He added that COSPEN would coordinate the mobilisation exercise through student union presidents across the various institutions. item.title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times
item.description: The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory. Jensen Huang, chief executive of the US-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan “under a standard business visitor status” and there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan’s parliament in response to lawmakers’ questions about Alice Huang’s entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements. “At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information,” Chiu said. “If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management.” Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said. “If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review,” Chiu said. “For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country.” The government has said Taiwan’s security agencies are investigating the incident. Cabinet spokeswoman Michelle Lee said Thursday “there is currently no public information” about whether Alice Huang “is suspected of any criminal offence or on the related investigative procedures”. “If a criminal offence is involved, due to the principle of prosecutorial confidentiality during an ongoing investigation, we cannot provide any further comment,” Lee said. Alice Huang was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. item.title: 2027: INEC must earn voters’ trust before election day — IPC

The Executive Director of IPC, Dr. Lanre Arogundade, said public trust in the commission must be established long before election day, warning that misinformation, disinformation and inaccurate communication could undermine the credibility of the electoral process. Arogundade spoke on Wednesday in Kano at a two-day capacity-building engagement for INEC’s Voter Education and Publicity (VEP) and gender officials on electoral trust, effective communication, legal literacy and voter engagement. item.title: Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President
item.description: Two members of France’s elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source. As is customary for the arrival of foreign heads of state, the Republican Guards formed an honour guard in full ceremonial dress with sabres for the arrival of Slovak President Peter Pellegrini late Wednesday. One guard can be seen swaying before crashing to the ground, falling against a pillar at the Elysee Palace as his ceremonial sword clattered to the ground. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (R) bids farewell to Slovakia’s President Peter Pellegrini following their meeting at the Elysee presidential Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP Aides and Macron immediately rushed towards the stricken guard, images from an AFP photographer showed. Le Parisien daily said that a second guard collapsed off camera, with Macron looking concerned and then hurriedly welcoming his Slovak counterpart. A French presidential source, who asked not to be named, told AFP that both guards had suffered from “fainting attacks” and no other comment would be made. “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine,” added the source. The Republican Guard, part of the French gendarmerie, is responsible for guards of honour in France, which often involve standing for long periods in heavy clothing while holding their sword vertically. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (L) and other officials attend to a Republican Guard who fainted while standing at attention, as he waits the arrival of Slovakia’s President at the Elysee Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. item.title: SQI College of ICT announces second convocation for November 21
item.description: SQI College of ICT has announced November 21, 2026, for its second convocation ceremony, with a focus on the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital skills in shaping the future. The ceremony, scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. at the institution’s main campus along Old Ilorin Road, opposite Yoaco Filling Station, Ogbomoso, Oyo State, will bring together graduating students, academics, technology professionals, industry leaders and other stakeholders. The event will be held under the theme, “Audacity to Reimagine the Future with Artificial Intelligence, Digital Skills and Human Possibilities.” The institution said the theme reflects the transformative impact of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies on society, while highlighting the need to combine technological advancement with human creativity, innovation and relevant skills to shape the future. The ceremony is expected to attract personalities from various sectors, including academics, technology experts, industry leaders and professionals. Graduating students, parents, guardians, members of the Governing Council and Board of Trustees are also expected to attend. Established to bridge the gap between conventional education and industry demands, SQI College of ICT has continued to emphasise practical learning, hands-on training and industry-relevant skills development. The institution said its academic approach goes beyond conventional classroom instruction to incorporate real-world projects, practical assignments and experiential learning aimed at equipping students with the skills to address industry challenges and compete in the global digital economy. Its academic offerings include Computer Science + AI, Accountancy + AI, and Business Administration and Management + AI, alongside specialised training in Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Data Analysis, Cybersecurity, Visual Design, Product Design and Cloud Computing. Through these programmes, the institution seeks to produce graduates capable of translating theoretical knowledge into practical solutions, developing technology-driven products and contributing to the digital transformation of businesses and society. Beyond the conferment of academic awards, the second convocation is expected to provide opportunities for networking, knowledge exchange and collaboration among academics, industry professionals, technology enthusiasts and emerging talents. The Rector, on behalf of the Governing Council and Board of Trustees, has invited parents, industry partners, members of the public and well-wishers to join the institution in celebrating the graduating students and the milestone in its development. The institution said the ceremony would further demonstrate its commitment to technology education, digital skills development and the preparation of a new generation of professionals for opportunities in the global digital economy. item.title: Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike
item.description: Government workers in Osun resumed duty on Thursday after putting off their three-day warning strike called by the organiser labour for the release of funds due to local governments in the state by the Federal Government. The News of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates of the state government secretariat in Abere and Osun Assembly, shut since Monday, were reopened with workers back to work. Similarly, workers in Olorunda and Osogbo Local Government Secretariats were also back to their duty posts. NAN reports that organised labour in the state had on Sunday directed workers to embarked on solidarity strike with local government workers for the release of the withheld council allocations. The organised labour comprising the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC) and Joint Negotiating Council (JNC), however, on Wednesday directed workers to resume duty today. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. item.title: Sales Hack Conference 2026: Nnamani leads six industry experts to Abuja
item.description: By Chioma Okoye The Convener of the Sales Hack Conference, Chinedu Paul Nnamani, is set to bring together six professionals from the business, technology, entrepreneurship, media and management sectors for the 2026 edition of the conference scheduled to hold in Abuja on Saturday, November 14. The conference, themed “Explosive Sales: Market Smart, Convert More, Earn Big,” is aimed at equipping entrepreneurs, business owners, marketers and sales professionals with practical strategies for improving sales performance, attracting customers and growing sustainable businesses. According to the organisers, the conference is designed to provide a platform for sharing practical business knowledge, professional experience and industry insights to help individuals and organisations strengthen their sales capabilities. item.title: Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick
item.description: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” the club said in a statement. It added: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.” Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins in all competitions. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago. The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. Established in the year 2000, the ACF, a socio-cultural organisation which draws its membership from the 19 northern states, seeks to protect the interests of Northern Nigeria.
